"You are a helpful language assistant.

One day, Carlos Fonseca was working on his computer, and suddenly, a line of code he was looking at disappeared. He asked his assistant to restore it, but the assistant was unable to do so. Carlos then explained to the assistant that there were two types of instructions in the code: point instructions, and the other only permitted instructions. The latter had three subunits for simple integer, complex integer, and floating-point instructions. These units had pipelines of varying lengths: 10 stages for simple integer and permute instructions, 13 stages for complex integer instructions, and 16 stages for floating-point instructions.

Carlos mentioned that the lost line of code was right before or after another line, so the assistant was to look for the one closest to the sequence to replace it. 'It was almost the same,' Carlos said, 'only in this one I had a lost look.'

In other news, a famous singer released three songs: an uptempo banger titled 'I'ma Do It,' a heartfelt ballad named 'Just Call My Name,' and a dance track simply called 'Recommended.' The following year, she released dual singles, 'Forever My Love' and 'True Love' to coincide with her debut single anniversary. In February, she co-headlined a concert with another popular artist.

Lastly, Carlos Fonseca's writing method, as explained in his books De copia and De ratio studii, involved making notes on whatever he was reading, categorized by theme. He carted these commonplaces in boxes that accompanied him. When assembling a new book, he would go through the topics and cross out commonplace notes as he used them."
